status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026 and not yet checked by the translation workers. Vocabulary follows the course: auto, autobus.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Double Letters, Part 1
lessons.description: A doubled consonant is held longer, and it changes the word. Hear pala against palla, and caro against carro.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Letters C and G, Part 1
lessons.description: C and G are hard before a, o, and u, and soft before e and i. Hear casa against cena, and gatto against gelato.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Gn and Gli, Part 1
lessons.description: Gn sounds like the ny in canyon, and gli like the lli in million. Hear bagno, gnocchi, figlio, and famiglia.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Accent Marks, Part 1
lessons.description: An accent mark can be the only thing that tells two words apart. Compare e with è, and la with là.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb andare, to go, changes to say who is going. Spot what changes: vado, vai, va, andiamo.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 2
lessons.description: More of andare, to go: for all of you, for them, for "let's", and for what you are off to do.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One, Part 1
lessons.description: For more than one, the last vowel changes, and so does the word for the: il cane becomes i cani, and la casa becomes le case.

lessons.title: Patterns - Words That Match, Part 1
lessons.description: A describing word matches the thing it describes: rosso with il libro, rossa with la casa. Spot the ending that changes.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: An Italian question usually has the same words in the same order as the statement. Only the voice rises.
words: This is the bus to Rome.
Is this the bus to Rome?

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: To say something is not so, put non in front of the verb. Nothing else in the sentence changes.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come After, Part 1
lessons.description: In English the describing word comes first: a white house. In Italian it usually comes after: una casa bianca.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Leaving Out I and You, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb's ending already says who is doing it, so Italian usually leaves out I, you, we, and they.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb andare, to go, at work in whole sentences. Spot vado, andiamo, vai, and vanno.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. Spot what the answer keeps from the question, and what it changes.
words: No, I do not speak English.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: Describing words matching what they describe, in whole sentences: bianca, rosse, alta, piccoli.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways: already done, happening now, and still to come.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
I am going to the market today.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
